note: Enntity/atlas inkling2/concurrent-spec-20261123: the Inkling 2 Mini (model type inkling2_loop) serving series, 62 commits merged up to Atlas-Inf main 7a717b659 (after #404 and #410). It parses the checkpoint as 48 unrolled layer visits, checks its layout at load, and adds the inkling-2-mini kernel target: decode attention with relative bias and per-token sinks, short convolutions with verify rollback, block attention residuals, loop message gates, NVFP4 and MXFP8 stacked-expert MoE decode, prefill experts at the checkpoint's declared numerics (W4A4 / W8A8 on the block-scaled tensor cores), GQA flash prefill attention, CUDA-graph single- and multi-sequence decode (BF16 projections of up to 8 rows on the batched GEMV, each row computed as the one-row GEMV computes it; with the checkpoint's weights a visit's input projections run as one launch), the Spark NVFP4 overlay for decode and verify (attention projections, the experts of layers 20-23, lm_head; prefill reads the checkpoint's own tensors in both modes), programmatic dependent launch for the target's kernels (always on), and the checkpoint's DSpark drafter on the DFlash head. The scheduler tracks the reasoning block and closes it with <|end_message|> once it runs past its effort's budget or loops (budget forcing). Tool-call arguments stream as they are generated for a request that asks (stream_tool_arguments: true), and the tool guard's stream setting checks such a call when it ends; every other request's calls are held until they pass. Prefix caching carries each visit's short-conv state on the cache's snapshots, a prompt under 512 tokens skips the tail-checkpoint split, an exact replay of a block-aligned prompt restores its tail checkpoint, a prompt that forks from a cached one can save a checkpoint at the fork (branch checkpoints, now for aux-state models too), and the disk tier restores evicted KV only up to a snapshot; the checkpoint's vision tower (a 23-layer ViT with axial RoPE and layer scale on the shared ViT kernels, one image token per 40x40 pixel tile, no resize), with token embeddings normed once at load so image rows skip the embedding norm as in the reference. A call written with no block header (a forced tool choice) is read as the answer. With two live requests the DSpark proposes share one vocabulary-head pass, an operator depth table bounds their drafts, and a pair whose drafts stop paying decodes plain until a re-probe. The drafter reports each draft's confidence, so a verify can stop where it is unsure, and the rule that turns drafts off for a sequence weighs each step by the drafts it verified and waits a short time before its first re-probe. A verify run attends as decode rows do, so greedy text with the drafter on is the text without it. Three, five, six and seven sequences decode at their own width instead of padded to four or eight rows. A Spark decode row's input projections run as one launch. Every live sequence's drafts are proposed in one batched pass, and a verify keeps decode's arithmetic at any row count. Proposed upstream to Atlas-Inf. Window-bounded KV (Enntity/atlas inkling2/swa-kv-window-20261124, three commits on d3318e087): the 40 sliding-window layer visits keep only the rows their 1,024-token window reads, in a pool of their own mapped from each KV block, so context costs the 8 global visits' 32 KiB a token instead of 192 KiB; greedy text is identical to d3318e087 (attention reads the same rows in the same order), and snapshot windows stay pinned for prefix-cache resumes (up to an eighth of the KV budget). The disk tier (PREFIX_CACHE_DIR) keeps full-length KV. Merged with incoai's DFlash2 drafter for Inkling 2 Mini (Enntity/atlas inkling2/dflash2-drafter-20261124, two commits on d3318e087): its taps mapped as DSpark's, the target's final norm on the last tap, and a confidence twin of the DFlash2 selector for the Inkling target. Plus the closure-attestation fixes (Atlas-Inf #250, proposed as Atlas-Inf/atlas#419, and the kernel_source resolver fix stacked on it): the image's suite now runs the_baked_attestation_reproduces_from_the_tree for this one-model build instead of skipping it.
